chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'From the character/manners of the Prophets (peace be upon them) is the Siwak (brushing teeth with a twig)'.

key_terms.أَخْلَاقِ: Manners, character, or traits (plural of khuluq)
key_terms.السِّوَاكُ: Siwak, the act of cleaning teeth with a twig or brush

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and physical significance of Siwak in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the Siwak as a defining moral characteristic (akhlaq) of the Prophets, elevating it from mere hygiene to a spiritual practice that mirrors their purity. This narration, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on emulating the physical and spiritual habits of the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophets as a means of attaining closeness to God. The inclusion of Siwak among 'akhlaq' suggests it is an intrinsic part of the Prophetic demeanor rather than just a ritual act.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the mannerisms of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> is the brushing of teeth’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ’It is of the moral discipline of the prophets to brush one’s teeth.’”
